GB.summary:
- **Josh Jacobs (RB)** — He returned to a real practice and said he wants to play, but he also acknowledged the staff may limit him as he ramps up after two months away from football. For this week, he profiles as the most important backfield lever in Green Bay, but not necessarily a full workloads lock; his presence can push the Packers away from the recent committee. [1, 9]

- **Josh Jacobs / MarShawn Lloyd / Pierre Strong / Kaleb Johnson (RBs)** — With Chris Brooks still out, the Packers’ recent backfield rotation has been Lloyd as the carry leader, Strong handling a big share against Dallas, and Johnson barely playing after fumbling issues. Jacobs’ return threatens all three roles, especially the highest-value touches and goal-line work, even if the split is still unsettled. [1]

- **Bo Melton (WR) / Christian Watson / Matthew Golden / Savion Williams** — Melton was the only Packers receiver who didn’t practice, while Watson, Golden and Williams were limited. If Melton sits, the route tree narrows and the remaining healthy wideouts should soak up his snaps, with Watson and Golden the clearest fantasy beneficiaries. [5, 10]

- **Jordan Love (QB)** — Love moved to full participation after being limited Wednesday with a sore back, and the team expects him to play. That keeps Green Bay’s passing game in its normal shape this week and reduces concern that the offense will need to dial back the downfield plan. [9, 10]

- **Packers pass game vs. Lions deep coverage** — Green Bay already leans heavily on deep shots, and Detroit has been poor against passes thrown deep, which fits the skill set of Watson and Golden. In a game where the Lions may be forced to defend speed vertically, the Packers’ explosive-play receivers get a matchup boost. [12]
